summary:
Custody placement is the sharpest documented exposure for a trans visitor. German prisons run on a statutory separation with a binary men/women housing model, and assignment matching a prisoner's gender identity has been practised only in exceptional cases; several states have amended their prison statutes in recent years to accommodate legally recognised gender diversity, and a new § 17 of the Rhineland-Palatinate prison act took effect on 1 March 2026 with no press coverage at all.

How the exception is applied in practice is unsettled. In August 2025 the chief prosecutor for Halle stated that Marla-Svenja Liebich, whose gender entry was changed to female at the end of 2024 under the Self-Determination Act, would serve an 18-month sentence for incitement at Chemnitz women's prison with placement reviewed at intake. After her extradition from a neighbouring state in July 2026 she was transferred to a men's prison despite being legally registered as a woman since 2025, with authorities citing the safety of prisoners at the women's facility; critics called her gender change an abuse of the self-determination law. A Verfassungsblog essay from March 2026 argues that trans prisoners need no discriminatory special law and that ordinary anti-discrimination law should govern their placement and treatment.

Airport screening is the other documented point of friction. The trans DJ and producer BASHKKA filed a legal complaint under the Equal Treatment Act over a screening at Frankfurt Airport on 23 November 2024, alleging that officers deliberately disregarded her gender identity in a targeted, degrading act of transphobic harassment; she provided Resident Advisor a copy of her statement to the airport.

Women-only venues remain contested but the dispute is confined to commercial leisure settings. A guideline from the Deutscher Sauna-Bund issued in January 2025 restricting women's saunas to persons whose primary sex characteristics correspond set off a public argument about registered trans women's access, and Berlin saunas and comparable venues have been working out how to treat trans women since the Self-Determination Act took effect on 1 January 2025 after months of argument over women-protected spaces and fears the self-declaration route would be misused. Trans woman Alessia Dorigo countered that claiming a trans identity on a whim is unrealistic, that identity is felt rather than declared, and that she had taken a hard road to it.
tangentialFactors:
National policy moved against LGBTI interests during 2025 on three fronts. In June the Federal Cabinet proposed designating Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia as safe countries of origin despite LGBTI people facing imprisonment there. In July the Education Minister banned gender-inclusive language in her ministry, a step the Federal Anti-Discrimination Office said contradicts constitutional equality protection. In August the Merz coalition announced that it would end humanitarian admission programmes including the Afghanistan scheme for persecuted LGBTI people.

The German STOP the HATE campaign, run by a prevention and empowerment organisation in northern Germany, maintains a practical resource directory: a counselling finder sorted by topic, emergency guidance including an LSBTIQ* crisis line, and a hate-crime knowledge base covering underreporting (the Dunkelziffer), evidence preservation, witness support and reporting channels.
localsOnly:
The Berlin prison service publishes an official page, in German, with information for trans, inter and non-binary persons in custody, setting out the rules and contacts that apply across Berlin facilities.

The Criminological Research Institute of Lower Saxony (KFN) documents the statutory basis of the binary model, citing § 170(2) of the Lower Saxony correctional act, and runs a research project on the situation of transgender people in prison.

A DW feature of 23 August 2023 reported that German prisons offer few safe spaces for trans inmates, describing the case of climate activist Penelope Frank of Last Generation, legally recorded male, who faced assignment to a men's prison if convicted, and confirming that housing runs on a binary men/women model with gender-identity-conforming placement only exceptional.
outOfScopeNotes:
The France24 link on the male-prison transfer was not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the July 2026 article it points to concerns the same case covered by DW, and only the headline premise is recorded here.

The Tagesspiegel Queerspiegel article on Berlin sauna practice has a paywalled body; only the lede was captured, so the substance of how individual venues apply the Self-Determination Act is unverified.

Whether the Chemnitz women's prison placement announced in August 2025 was final, and whether any challenge to the July 2026 transfer succeeded, is not established by these sources; the DW and France24 items rest on a single case.

The DW prison description predates the Self-Determination Act, in force since 1 January 2025, so the account of routine practice may be outdated, and the statutory citation is specific to one province while placement rules and their application vary by state.
